subject: DPA: subprocessor access boundaries & product evaluation impact
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@clarityhealth.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA: subprocessor access boundaries & product evaluation impact

Hi Elena —

Thanks for sending your redlines. We reviewed the DPA plus the subprocessor appendix and have a few cross-functional asks before we can sign:

1) Subprocessor runtime access: the current redline would allow certain third-party telemetry and monitoring vendors to receive inference request metadata (timestamps, model id, host region). Product needs to confirm whether exposing model id + request timing to vendors is OK for our evaluation pipelines. That data influences auto-scaling/latency analysis and we typically restrict model id exposure.

2) KV cache snapshot clause: Security raised a flag about the proposed clause that allows customer-delivered tooling to pull aggregated KV cache snapshots for debugging. We need a narrower scope or explicit authorization flow.

3) Analytics carve-out: Laura, can you confirm whether we can accept the "anonymized usage metrics" language without a per-customer opt-out? Product may need an opt-out checkbox for regulated accounts.

Attached: clarity_dpa_redline_v3.docx (with inline comments) and subprocessor_access_matrix.csv (current vendor list + roles).

Proposed next steps:
- Product (Laura) to advise on model id exposure and a mitigated language suggestion by EOD 3/18.
- Security (Olga) to propose a hardened KV-snapshot authorization flow by 3/19.
- If all agree, Legal will prepare a DocuSign-ready DPA and we can route to Clarity for signature.

Elena — would you be able to accept a restricted-access wording for telemetry vendors and an explicit authorization requirement for KV snapshots? If not, please flag which parts are non-starters.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0146

From: Elena Park <elena.park@clarityhealth.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: ClarityHealth Legal <legal@clarityhealth.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: subprocessor access boundaries & product evaluation impact

Camila —

Thanks for the quick read. We understand product and security concerns and want to move fast; ClarityHealth is sensitive to any restriction that would prevent our ops vendor (Velox Monitoring) from getting request-level timing for SLA reconciliation.

Specific asks from our side:
- Velox needs request timestamps and host-region to match against our internal logs. We can accept a hashed model identifier but cannot accept model-level redaction for our internal audit needs.
- KV cache access is a blocker for us only in the case of full raw snapshots. If Redwood can provide a scoped debug export (timeboxed, read-only, anonymized user ids), that would be workable.

I can ask Legal to suggest concrete language if that helps — they prefer the velocity to avoid holding up our pilot contract.

Best,
Elena Park
Director of IT Ops | ClarityHealth
elena.park@clarityhealth.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: DPA: subprocessor access boundaries & product evaluation impact

Quick notes from Product:

- Model identifier: Product can accept a hashed model id (HMAC with per-customer salt) for external vendors. That preserves our internal naming schema while enabling Clarity to correlate events. We will supply an example hashing spec for legal to include.

- KV cache debug export: Product is uncomfortable with a blanket right to pull KV snapshots. Proposed change: vendor debug exports must be:
  * Generated by Redwood runtime only upon customer authorization (explicit form + audit trail)
  * Time-limited (maximum 72 hours of retained debug artifact)
  * Scrubbed for PHI (we will run our PII scrubbing step for exports to external vendors)

- Analytics opt-out: Product will expose an account-level toggle for telemetry sharing, but enterprise customers can request a contractual carve-out. Laura to work with Olga and Legal on the precise opt-out wording.

I will attach the hashing spec and a draft snippet for the KV export flow by EOD.

Laura Bennett
Head of Product — Inference Platform | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: DPA: subprocessor access boundaries & product evaluation impact

Security's position:

- KV snapshot: we will not permit full raw snapshots to external subprocessors. The authorization flow Laura suggested is acceptable provided we document: who requested export, justification, who approved, TTL of artifact, and S3 location with KMS-wrapped encryption. Exports will be logged and immutable.

- Telemetry vendor fields: hashed model id + host region + request timestamp is OK if:
  * hashing algorithm is provably collision-resistant and keys are rotated quarterly,
  * Clarity signs an appendix committing to not attempt to reverse the mapping,
  * any aggregated logs shared with vendors exclude user-level identifiers unless customer explicitly authorizes.

- Audit evidence: for Clarity's compliance needs, we can provide a short-form audit package (export of logs showing the authorization flow and export event) but will not provide raw inference payloads.

I will produce a Security-approved paragraph for the DPA and the KV export SOP by EOD 3/19.

Olga Petrov
Director, Product Security | Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai

1) Hashed model id spec (Product)
2) KV export authorization flow & TTL (Security)
3) Telemetry opt-out / enterprise carve-out process (Product + Legal)

If Clarity can accept the hashed model id and the restricted export flow, we can route the DPA for signature today.

Josh — I looped you in so Velox Monitoring is aware of the hashed-id approach and the audit package we will provide. Can you coordinate with Velox to confirm they can operate with a hashed id and the 72-hour export TTL?

Action items:
